name: baked potato
rationale: earthy (geosmin) is dominant; classifier missed it, only got roasted skin

name: black bean
rationale: earthy raw, roasted pyrazines when cooked

name: caramel
rationale: literally the definition: HMF + furaneol + maltol

name: chestnut
rationale: starchy nut; roasted develops Maillard, not creamy/lactonic

name: chickpea
rationale: raw is earthy/beany; classifier hit only roasted

name: coriander
rationale: linalool + alpha-pinene + geranyl acetate — NOT pungent

name: corn
rationale: fresh corn: DMS (pungent), hexanal (green), lactones (creamy); all valid

name: fenugreek
rationale: sotolone is the marker compound — curry/maple = caramel family

name: flour
rationale: raw flour is earthy/starchy; only becomes roasted when toasted

name: garam masala
rationale: spice blend; warm/caramel vs roasted depending on toasting

name: gruyere
rationale: aged hard cheese; lactic + butyric + free fatty acids

name: hazelnut
rationale: filbertone + pyrazines; almost always roasted in use

name: hoisin sauce
rationale: fermented soy base; aged is dominant — classifier missed it

name: lentil
rationale: raw lentils are earthy/beany; classifier overshot to roasted

name: marjoram
rationale: cis-sabinene hydrate + terpinenes — terpene-herbal, not green-leafy

name: miso
rationale: fermented soy paste; aged with Maillard from brewing

name: nigella seed
rationale: thymoquinone + p-cymene + slight peppery nasal note

name: nori
rationale: seaweed; sometimes toasted but marine is dominant

name: olive
rationale: oleocanthal + leaf aldehydes; not creamy in dairy sense

name: parmesan
rationale: aged hard cheese; lactic + butyric + propionic

name: pumpkin pie spice
rationale: cinnamon/clove/nutmeg blend = caramel-adjacent; classifier got it badly wrong

name: sausage
rationale: cooked meat = Maillard dominant; classifier picked up seasoning herbs

name: shallot
rationale: allium; same sulfur chemistry as onion

name: shrimp
rationale: TMA + bromophenols; not creamy unless butter-cooked

name: sweet potato
rationale: maltol/furaneol when cooked + beta-ionone + earthy base

name: tofu
rationale: very mild; hexanal-green and slight earthy both apply

name: worcestershire sauce
rationale: fermented anchovy + vinegar + molasses; aged dominant

name: black lime
rationale: dried/aged lime — all three chemistries present
